title: Build a standard SKU key
summary: Compose a clean SKU key from messy parts with TRIM, UPPER, LEFT, RIGHT and &, then check for duplicates with COUNTIF.

blocks.text: Merchandising wants one standard SKU key for every size of every style, so that sales, stock and the price list can all be joined on the same text. The raw parts arrive separately: a category name typed any way, a style number without leading zeros, and a size.

In this capstone for the text missions you will clean and join those parts into one key, such as SNE-450-42, and then count duplicates. Two rows with the same key would double count stock, so duplicates must be found before the key is used.

items: Objective: combine TRIM, UPPER, LEFT, RIGHT and & to build a key, and find duplicates with COUNTIF.
You pass the mission at 75% or more in the Assessment.

blocks.text: Clean the category with TRIM, take the first three letters with LEFT, put them in capitals with UPPER, then join a hyphen, the padded style number, another hyphen and the size.

Padding trick: joining 000 in front makes the text longer (45 becomes 00045), and RIGHT keeps only the last three characters (045). A style that already has three digits, such as 450, comes out unchanged.
COUNTIF counts the cells in the range that equal D2. The count always includes D2 itself, so more than 1 means the key appears again somewhere else.

items: In this list COUNTIF($D$2:$D$6,"SNE-450-42") is 3, so each of those rows is a Duplicate. COUNTIF ignores upper and lower case.
Use >1, not >0: every key is counted once for itself, so a count of 1 means it is unique.
Fix the range with $ signs ($D$2:$D$6) so it does not slide down when you copy the formula.
Build long formulas in pieces, in helper cells, then join the pieces. Check each part with LEN.

blocks.text: Use the key list from Training (D2:D6). Type numbers without commas or spaces, for example 12.

items: Clean the parts first: TRIM for spaces, UPPER for case, LEFT and RIGHT to take pieces.
RIGHT("000"&n,3) pads a number to three digits with leading zeros.
Join the parts with & and put the fixed hyphens in double quotes.
COUNTIF(range,key)>1 flags duplicates because each key counts itself once.

blocks.text: A clean, standard key is the foundation of every reliable join in merchandising reporting.

items.prompt: Why does the key formula join "000" in front of the style number before using RIGHT?

options.label: So every style number has exactly three characters, with leading zeros where needed
To make the style number three times bigger

items.prompt: What does =COUNTIF(D2:D6,"SNE-450-42") return for the key list in Training?
Why does the duplicate check test COUNTIF(...)>1 and not COUNTIF(...)>0?

options.label: Because every key is counted once for itself, so a count of 1 means the key is unique
Because COUNTIF starts counting at zero
Because the range has one blank cell
